There, section 4. The oil remaining on the eighth day from the oil needed for the measure of lighting, etc. Note: regarding what everyone asked as a contradiction in the words of Shulchan Aruch, see the Chanukah discourse of the year 5601, where I wrote to resolve this by distinguishing between a matter of prohibition and a matter of mitzvah; see there, with Hashem's help. Regarding what everyone asked as a contradiction between the words of Shulchan Aruch here and above, siman 672, Turei Zahav brought in the name of Mahari to answer that here it is speaking where he placed the oil without specification, and above it is speaking where he stipulated that it was only for the measure of lighting. Turei Zahav wondered from the Talmud in chapter Nigmar Hadin, that what is not fit for him is not seized by it; and just as this is so for Abaye regarding designation, the same applies for Rava regarding an act. We already wrote above about this. Now it seems as follows, based on what we already proved in our novellae to the laws of Sukkah, which are still in manuscript, to prove against Hagahos Ashri brought by Magen Avraham, who holds that the sukkah is not forbidden until one sits in it, because designation is not significant. I proved from what is said: if one set aside seven esrogim for seven days, he fulfills with each one and eats it the next day. If we say that designation is not significant in this case, then at twilight it was not muktzeh, and if so there is no muktzeh for half of Shabbos; why should it not be permitted immediately? Perforce, in this case designation is significant. The reason appears to be that since the sukkah is forbidden for benefit by force of the verse, the festival of Sukkos, just as the festival offering is to Hashem, etc., and regarding designation and inherent sanctity, designation is significant, as Magen Avraham wrote in siman 42, so too with the sukkah. The same applies to lulav, since we derive lulav from sukkah; see there. If so, according to this, the same applies to the Chanukah lamp, since it is like the Menorah, as Rashi wrote, beginning with lighting performs the mitzvah: it is like the Menorah. Therefore here too designation is significant, as with inherent sanctity. Therefore it is well understood. Certainly according to Abaye, regarding designation alone, since it is only speech and not an act, we say that what is not fit for him is not seized by it. The same applies to an act according to Rava in cases where designation is not significant: since there is only an act here, we say that for what is fit for him it is considered an act, but for what is not fit for him the act is not considered an act. What is extra is as though it is not there, and in the whole of it no act was done in the extra portion at all. The act on the part that was fit does not work to forbid the part that was not fit. But here with oil, since designation alone also forbids it, then at the time of the act the designation takes effect on all of it, for we did not know whether he would need it or not, and on which part the name leftover would fall. If so, designation takes effect on all of it. Then, if afterward he also performs an act, since here there is both an act and designation, all of it is forbidden. In this case, the act on part of it is effective for all of it, because in any event he designated all of it for this, and it becomes like one body; the act on part of it is effective for all of it because it became one through designation. Designation is effective at least to make it one matter and not a separate matter. Then, since he performed an act with part of it that was fit for him, and that was a strong act, this is effective for all of it and all of it becomes forbidden. In this everyone agrees, and the words of the Mechaber are well understood. According to this, there is no need to say that there it is speaking where he stipulated. Rather, even without stipulation, there it is speaking where he did not designate it first, and it has only an act; therefore it follows the reasoning of Turei Zahav, that what is not fit for him is not seized by it. But here it is speaking where he first designated all of it and afterward kindled it. With designation together with the act, all of it is forbidden. Therefore the She'iltos, which is the source of this law, and all the authorities, were precise and concluded, because it was set aside for its mitzvah. Why do I need all this? This is already known, that for this reason it was forbidden initially. Rather, the intent is to teach that he set it aside initially for this, so it was also designation. Therefore it concluded, because he set it aside for its mitzvah from the beginning, and this is designation together with the act; and it is well understood. Examine this, for so my view now inclines. There is support for the above distinction from what we hold in Choshen Mishpat, siman 275, section 7, and in Sema there, that when one takes possession of the property of a convert who died without heirs, he acquires only as far as a team of oxen goes and returns. But if it is called by the name of the convert, he acquires all of it; see there. Thus, if it is not called by the name of the convert, the act of taking possession is effective only for itself and not for the other fields; but if it is called by the name of the convert, the act of taking possession is effective for all of it, for everything called by his name; see there. If so, here too, if designation is significant and all of it is called the Chanukah lamp, the subsequent act with part of the oil that burned is effective, and it is as if an act was done with all the oil, so there is a strong act here. But if he did not designate it, the act done with the oil is not effective for what remains; examine this. Also what Magen Avraham and Pri Chadash wrote, that it is forbidden to keep them for the next year because of concern for a mishap, is difficult: what proof is there from those other cases? There, the prohibition is Torah law, and therefore they decreed because of concern for a mishap. But Chanukah itself is rabbinic prohibition; why should we be concerned for a mishap? It would be a decree upon a decree. But see the Chanukah discourse that I cited above; there I also proved from this that they treated it exactly like Torah law because of the blessing; see there and examine. Now regarding leftover oil in the Chanukah lamp, whether one may light it in the synagogue in order to pray by it: it seems obvious that it is permitted. Although it is forbidden for benefit, nevertheless we hold that mitzvos were not given for benefit. Not only according to those who hold that even rabbinic mitzvos were not given for benefit, but even according to those who hold that rabbinic mitzvos were given for benefit, that is only regarding whether a Torah-level prohibition of benefit is involved; in that case we follow the Torah level, for he is not obligated by the Torah in this mitzvah, and if so he benefits by Torah law, like one who receives reward as one who is not commanded yet performs. But regarding a rabbinic prohibition of benefit, certainly it is permitted to fulfill with it one of their mitzvos from either side: if we follow Torah law, it is entirely permitted; and if we follow rabbinic law, then rabbinically he is commanded in this, and something in which he is commanded is upon him like a yoke and was not given for benefit. If so, the Chanukah lamp, which is rabbinic, may be used for a mitzvah use. Moreover, even regarding the Chanukah lamp itself, some permit a sacred use. Even those who forbid it there do so only while it is burning for the mitzvah of the Chanukah lamp, for then one may say that if he uses it for holiness, it is not recognizable that it was kindled for the mitzvah. Or one may say that it is a disgrace to the mitzvah, for moving from mitzvah to mitzvah can also involve disgrace. But if something already remains from the Chanukah lamp, which they burn by itself, a recognizable sign is certainly not needed in this. Nor does disgrace of the mitzvah apply, for if he burns it just so, that is a greater disgrace, since he burns it only because it is forbidden for benefit. That is a greater disgrace to the mitzvah than lighting it in the synagogue. See also what Turei Zahav wrote similarly above in siman 154, that even for an item that is forbidden to lower from its sanctity, this is only if it is still fit for its mitzvah; but if it is not fit for its mitzvah, it is better to use it for a lesser mitzvah than to bury it as it is. If so, all the more so here, it is better to use it for the sake of holiness than to bury it as it is. This is obvious in my view, and I would not have needed to put it in writing. But since I saw that Pri Megadim in Mishbetzos wrote the opposite, and permitted only by adding to it and because of a double doubt, I wrote this to remove that thought from the heart of that sefer. With pardon to his honored Torah, he erred greatly in this and did not consider all that I wrote; see there and examine.
There, in the same aforementioned section. There is one who says that one may not add to it in order to nullify it. Note: see what I wrote to resolve this in a responsum in the year 5593, in Shulchan Aruch Yoreh Deah, siman 69, concerning goose fat; see there and examine well.

eliyah_rabbah.he: [ד] [לבוש] הרשות בידו וכו'. וכן נוהגין (רמ"א), ורש"ל סימן פ"ה פסק כבית יוסף שאין לו לברך אם לא כשאין ידוע שהדליקה עליו, ומזה קשה לי על שער אפרים סימן מ"ב שכתב שבית יוסף לטעמיה דכל בני ביתו מדליקין אחת, אבל למנהגא דידן לכולי עלמא צריך לברך דהוא בכלל המהדרין עד כאן הא רש"ל פסק מנהגא דידן וכן במטה משה ושל"ה, ואפילו הכי פסקו כבית יוסף, ועוד הא בתשובת מהרי"ל סימן קנ"ו ובמהרי"ל כתב להאי דנהיגי להדליק כל אחד מבני ביתו וכו' משום ברכה לבטלה אין כאן כיון דאינו רוצה לצאת בשל אשתו, עד כאן, תיפוק ליה דהוא מן המהדרין כמו שאר בני ביתו, גם כתבתי בסימן תרע"א ס"ק ב' דאיש ואשתו אינו בכלל מהדרין דכגוף אחד דמיין. ולדינא פסק של"ה כשידוע שמדליקין בביתו יעמוד אצל בעל הבית כשמברך ויענה אמן, ואם כבר הדליק בעל הבית יברך בלא שם מלכות וכן פסק מטה משה, ואני אומר דאין למחות מנהגינו וכמו שהעידו מהרי"ו ומהרי"ל שהבאתי:
eliyah_rabbah.en: Levush: Permission is in his hand, etc. And so is the practice; Rema. Maharshal, siman 85, ruled like Beis Yosef that he should not bless unless it is not known that she kindled for him. From this I find difficulty with Shaar Ephraim, siman 42, who wrote that Beis Yosef follows his own view that all members of the household kindle one lamp, but according to our custom, everyone agrees that he must bless, for he is included among those who beautify the mitzvah. Until here. But Maharshal ruled according to our custom, and so did Mateh Moshe and Shnei Luchos HaBris, and even so they ruled like Beis Yosef. Furthermore, in Responsa Maharil, siman 156, and in Maharil, he wrote about those who practice that each member of the household kindles, etc., that there is no blessing in vain, since he does not want to fulfill his obligation with that of his wife. Until here. Let him instead say that he is among those who beautify the mitzvah, like the other members of his household. I also wrote in siman 671, paragraph 2, that a man and his wife are not included in the category of mehadrin, for they are considered like one body. As a matter of law, Shnei Luchos HaBris ruled that when it is known that they kindle in his home, he should stand near the homeowner when he blesses and answer amen. If the homeowner already kindled, he should bless without the Name and kingship; and so ruled Mateh Moshe. But I say that one should not protest our custom, as Mahariv and Maharil, whom I cited, testified.

levushei_serad.he: <small>סק"ד</small> כמ"ש ססי' תרע"א וכו'. בחצר שיש בה ב' פתחים מדליק בשתיהן ואין מברך רק באחד ולא בהשני כיון שאינו רק משום חשד. ויש לחלק דהתם שאני שכבר בירך בפתח אחד משא"כ כאן ואף שבעה"ב בירך הא בס"ג בהג"ה כ' שיכול לומר איני יוצא בברכת בעה"ב כ"ש שלא שותף בפרוטה:
levushei_serad.en: {Rama: s.k. 4} As siman 671, etc. In courtyard with two openings — kindle at both, bless only at one not second since only suspicion. One may distinguish: there different since already blessed at one opening — not so here; even though homeowner blessed — in seif 3 Hagahah wrote one may say I do not fulfill through homeowner's blessing — all the more if not partnered with perutah.

machatzit_hashekel.he:
(ס"ק ד) להדליק כו' כמ"ש סי' תרע"א היינו בחצר שי"ל שני פתחים שצ"ל בשניהם משום חשד. מ"מ אינו מברך כי אם על א':
ויש לחלק דהתם באמת מה שמדליק ברוח שני אין בו חיוב כ"א משום חשד. משא"כ הכא ניהו דאי משתתף עם בע"ה אין עליו חיוב מן הדין כ"א משום חשד. אבל השתא דמדליק בפני עצמו ודאי דאינו משתתף וא"כ חייב מצד הדין ולכן יברך. ועיין סעיף ג' ר"ל דבטור כתב דאפי' מדליקים עליו תוך ביתו מ"מ אם י"ל פתח פתוח לעצמו צריך להדליק מפני החשד וכה"ג שפיר י"ל דלא יברך דהא כה"ג פטור מצד הדין ואין מדליק כ"א מפני החשד. ולכן רמז מ"א לעיין בסעיף ג' שכתב רמ"א דאם הדליקו עליו תוך ביתו ואינו רוצה לצאת בהדלקת ביתו ורוצ' להדליק במקום שהוא ולברך רשאי. אם כן גם כהאי גוונא רשאי לברך אם י"ל פתח פתוח לעצמו אע"פ שהדליקו עליו בביתו דיכוין שלא לצאת בהדלקת ביתו ועיין שם ס"ג:
machatzit_hashekel.en:
Paragraph 4: To kindle, etc. As written in siman 671, namely regarding a courtyard that has two entrances, where one must kindle at both because of suspicion. Nevertheless, he blesses only over one.
And one may distinguish, for there, in truth, what he kindles in the second direction has no obligation except because of suspicion. This is not so here. Granted, if he participates with the homeowner, there is no obligation upon him by the strict law except because of suspicion. But now that he kindles for himself, he certainly is not participating, and if so he is obligated by the strict law; therefore he blesses. See section 3. Meaning: in the Tur he wrote that even if they kindle for him inside his home, nevertheless if he has an entrance open for himself, he must kindle because of suspicion. In that kind of case, one can properly say that he should not bless, for in that case he is exempt by the strict law and kindles only because of suspicion. Therefore Magen Avraham hinted to see section 3, where Rema wrote that if they kindled for him inside his home and he does not want to fulfill through the lighting of his home, but wants to kindle in the place where he is and bless, he may do so. If so, also in such a case he may bless if he has an entrance open for himself, even though they kindled for him at home, because he can intend not to fulfill through the lighting in his home. See there, section 3.

magen_avraham.he:
הצריך לשיעור הדלקה. דביותר משיעור הדלקה מותר להשתמש בו לכתחלה כמ"ש סי' תרע"ב ס"ב (ב"י מרדכי ורש"ל וש"ג) וב"ח פסק כשנתן השמן בסתם הוקצ' כל השמן וכ"מ בהג"מ ובר"ן ובתוס' שבת דף מ"ד ומיהו אין מוכרח כל כך ולכן טוב להתנות לכתחלה שלא יאסר אלא כשיעור וכתב הש"ג צ"ע אם נתן השמן שיעור חצי שעה ודלק יותר מחצי שעה אם מותר להסתפק ממנו:
ושורפו. ואסור להניחו בכלי מאוס לשהותו לשנה הבאה דחיישינן לתקלה (טור יש"ש) ועבי"ד סי' נ"ז:
שאין להוסיף וכו'. ול"ד לסי' תק"ז ס"ב דהתם אין נהנה ממנו עד אחר ביעורו משא"כ הכא דנהנה ממנו בשעת ביעורו אסור לבטלו (טור) ועבי"ד סי' צ"ט ס"ו דיש מתירין ולכן כ' כאן יש מי שאומר וכו' ועיין בש"ך שם ואפשר דהכא חמיר טפי כיון דהוי דשיל"מ דמדינא מותר לשהותו לשנה הבאה והוי דומיא דחמץ עבי"ד סי' ק"ב:
magen_avraham.en:
That is needed for the measure of lighting. For more than the measure of lighting, it is permitted to use it ab initio, as written in siman 672, section 2. Beis Yosef, Mordechai, Maharshal, and Shiltei Giborim. Bach ruled that when he placed the oil without specification, all the oil was set aside, and so it also seems in Hagahos Maimoniyos, Ran, and Tosafos, Shabbos 44. However, this is not so compelled. Therefore it is good to stipulate ab initio that only the measure should become forbidden. Shiltei Giborim wrote that it requires examination: if he placed enough oil for half an hour and it burned more than half an hour, whether one may use from it.
And burns it. It is forbidden to place it in a repulsive vessel to keep it until the following year, because we are concerned for a mishap. Tur, Yam Shel Shlomo. See Yoreh Deah, siman 57.
That one may not add, etc. It is not comparable to siman 507, section 2, for there he does not benefit from it until after its burning, whereas here he benefits from it at the time of its burning, and it is forbidden to nullify it. Tur. See Yoreh Deah, siman 99, section 6, where some permit; therefore here he wrote, there is one who says, etc. See Shach there. It is possible that here it is more severe, since it is something that has permitted status later, for by the strict law it is permitted to keep it until the following year, and it is comparable to chametz; see Yoreh Deah, siman 102.

mishnah_berurah.he:
(יז) הנותר ביום השמיני וכו' - דבלילות הקודמין אם נותר יכול להשתמש בהן למצות הדלקה בלילות שאחריהן ואם נתערב בשמן אחר דינו כדלקמיה:
(יח) מן השמן הצריך וכו' - היינו שלא נתן תחלה רק כשיעור הדלקה ונכבה באמצע ונותר ולכן אסור דהוקצה למצותו ואסור להנות הימנו אבל אם נתן הרבה בנר ונותר מותר להשתמש בו לכתחלה וכמו שכתב לעיל בסימן תרע"ב ס"ב. ודע דיש פוסקים שסוברין דאם נתן השמן בסתם הוקצה כל השמן אם לא דהתנה לכתחלה שלא יאסור אלא כשיעור ועיין לעיל בסימן תרע"ב במ"ב סק"ז:
(יט) ושורפו בפ"ע - דלהניחו לשנה הבאה לנ"ח אסור דחיישינן לתקלה ואפילו להניחו בכלי מאוס דודאי לא יבוא לאכלו ג"כ אסור דחיישינן שמא יבוא לדלוק ולהנות הימנו:
(כ) שאין להוסיף עליו וכו' - ועיין ביו"ד סימן צ"ט ס"ו דיש מתירין בכל איסור דרבנן להוסיף עליו אם נתערב ולכן כתב כאן יש מי שאומר:
mishnah_berurah.en:
That remains on the eighth day, etc. For on the earlier nights, if any remains, one may use it for the mitzvah of lighting on the following nights. If it became mixed with other oil, its law is as below.
From the oil needed, etc. This means that at first he placed only the measure needed for lighting, and it went out in the middle and some remained. Therefore it is forbidden, because it was set aside for its mitzvah and it is forbidden to benefit from it. But if he placed much oil in the lamp and some remained, it is permitted to use it ab initio, as written above in siman 672, section 2. Know that some authorities hold that if he placed the oil without specification, all the oil was set aside, unless he stipulated ab initio that only the measure should become forbidden. See above in siman 672 in Mishnah Berurah, paragraph 7.
And burns it by itself. For it is forbidden to leave it for the following year for the Chanukah lamp, because we are concerned for a mishap. Even to leave it in a repulsive vessel, so that he certainly will not come to eat it, is also forbidden, because we are concerned that he may come to light it and benefit from it.
That one may not add to it, etc. See Yoreh Deah, siman 99, section 6, where some permit adding to any rabbinic prohibition if it became mixed; therefore here he wrote, there is one who says.

peri_megadim.he: שאין עט״ז ובי״ד אות י״ב ובש״ך י״ט ועמ״א כאן אות י״ב והנה להוסיף יותר מששים ולהדליק בבית הכנסת ל״מ לכבוד די״ל דשרי אף בלא ביטול יותר מששים ואף להתפלל אצלו י״ל דשרי והוי ס״ס לקולא שמא הלכה דמותר להוסיף איסור דרבנן ושמא הלכה דתשמיש קדושה ללמוד ולהתפלל שרי כבסי׳ תרע״ג ועט״ז שם אות ד׳ ועדיין צ״ע ועא״ר כאן אות ז׳ ועמ״ש בפריי לי״ד שם ואם נאמר דממצוה למצוה שייך איסור עיין ר״ן בהא דמנר לנר מ״מ לכבוד הש״י בבית הכנסת ולא להתפלל אצלו י״ל דשרי לכ״ע וצ״ע:
peri_megadim.en: That one may not. See Turei Zahav and Yad, paragraph 12, and Shach, paragraph 19, and Magen Avraham here, paragraph 12. Now, to add more than sixty and kindle it in the synagogue for honor, one may say that it is permitted even without nullification in more than sixty. Even to pray near it, one may say it is permitted, and there is a double doubt for leniency: perhaps the halachah is that one may add to a rabbinic prohibition, and perhaps the halachah is that sacred use, to learn and pray, is permitted, as in siman 673. See Turei Zahav there, paragraph 4. Still, this requires examination. See Eliyah Rabbah here, paragraph 7, and what I wrote in my Pri on Yoreh Deah there. And if we say that from one mitzvah to another there is a prohibition, see Ran on the matter of lighting from lamp to lamp. Nevertheless, for the honor of Hashem in the synagogue, and not to pray beside it, one may say that it is permitted according to everyone; and this requires examination.

shaarei_teshuvah.he: בש"ע הנותר מן השמן כו' ועיין בספרי שו"ת בית אפרים מ"ש בזה להגאון בעמה"ת שאילת שלום ז"ל על השאלתות ועיין שם מ"ש בדברי הר"ן וה"ה ובדברי המ"א שכת' דהוי דשיל"מ ע"ש:
shaarei_teshuvah.en: In Shulchan Aruch: that which remains from the oil, etc. See my responsa Beis Ephraim, where I wrote about this to the great author of She'eilas Shalom, of blessed memory, regarding the She'iltos. See there, and what I wrote there concerning the words of Ran and Maggid Mishneh, and concerning the words of Magen Avraham, who wrote that it is something that has permitted status later; see there.

turei_zahav.he:
שאין להוסיף כו'. בי"ד סי' צ"ט ס"ו כתבתי שדברי הש"ע סותרים זא"ז בהוראה זו ושקי"ל להתיר כמ"ש הש"ע שם:
עושה לו מדורה. מה שקשה מכאן על מ"ש בסי' תרע"ב דמותר להשתמש בה אחר שדלק' כשיעור כתבתי שם:
turei_zahav.en:
That one may not add, etc. Yoreh De'ah siman 99 seif 6 I wrote Shulchan Aruch's words contradict in this ruling and halacha follows Shulchan Aruch there.
Makes bonfire for him. What is difficult from here on what written siman 672 permitted to use after kindled measure — I wrote there.

kaf_hachayyim.he: ד) כתב באגודה שמעתי מי ששותף עם חבירו לנ"ח צריך להוסיף מה שיתן לו חבירו ע"כ. וטעמו דאם לא ניכר שהוסיף בשביל חבירו איכא חשדא לומר שלא נשתתף ולפ"ז אפי' לא הוסיף כל מה שנתן לו אלא מקצת נמי סגי דניכר שנשתתף במה שהוסיף על מה שהיה רגיל. ב"ח. שכנה"ג בהגה"ט אות ב'. מ"א סק"א. ומיהו מדברי הא"ר אות ב' משמע שצריך שיתן בעה"ב שמן כשיעור חצי שעה בשביל האכסנאי כמ"ש א"א אות א' והפר"ח כתב דא"צ להוסיף בנר מה שנתן לו ומ"ש הב"ח להוסיף מקצת לא נהירא יעו"ש. אמנם דה"ח אות ב' פסק כדברי הב"ח דבעה"ב צריך להוסיף מעט שמן בשביל האורח חוץ השיעור שצריך ליתן לצורך חצי שעה. וכ"פ מ"ב אות ג' וכתב ודלא כהא"ר. וכ"נ משמעות הפו' שכתבו דסגי בפרוטה משמע דא"צ להוסיף בשביל האורח רק מעט יותר מכשיעור להיכרא בעלמא:
kaf_hachayyim.en: 4) The Agudah wrote: I heard that one who participates with another in a Chanukah light must add what his fellow gives him, end quote. His reason is that if it is not evident that he added oil for his fellow, there is a suspicion that he did not participate. According to this, even if he did not add all that his fellow gave him, but only some of it, that also suffices, since his participation is evident from what was added beyond his normal amount. Bach; Knesset HaGedolah in Hagahos HaTur, letter 2; Magen Avraham, s.k. 1. However, the words of Eliyah Rabbah, letter 2, imply that the homeowner must place oil sufficient to burn for half an hour on behalf of the lodger, as Eshel Avraham, letter 1, wrote. Pri Chadash wrote that he need not add to the light the value of what the lodger gave him, and that what the Bach wrote, that he must add a small amount, is not persuasive; see there. However, Derech HaChaim, letter 2, ruled in accordance with the Bach, that the homeowner must add a small amount of oil on behalf of the guest beyond the measure required to burn for half an hour. So too ruled Mishna Berurah, letter 3, and he wrote that this is unlike Eliyah Rabbah. This also appears to be the implication of the poskim who wrote that a perutah suffices, implying that he need add only a little beyond the required measure for the guest, merely as a recognizable indication.
